prompt:
In an experiment to determine the acceleration of free fall g using a simple pendulum, the period of oscillation T is related to the length L by T = 2 * pi * sqrt(L / g), which rearranges to g = (4 * pi^2 * L) / T^2.
The following measurements are recorded:
Length of pendulum L = (0.800 +/- 0.002) m
Time for 20 complete oscillations t_20 = (36.0 +/- 0.2) s

(a)(i) Calculate the period T of one oscillation and determine the absolute uncertainty delta T. [1]
(a)(ii) Calculate the percentage uncertainty in the length L and in the period T. [2]
(b)(i) Calculate the central value of g. [1]
(b)(ii) Calculate the percentage uncertainty in g. [1]
(b)(iii) Determine the absolute uncertainty in g and quote your final value in the form (g +/- delta g) m s^-2 with appropriate rounding. [1]

hints: Divide both the total time and its uncertainty by the number of oscillations (20).
mark_scheme: 1 mark: T = 1.80 s AND delta T = 0.01 s (or (1.80 +/- 0.01) s).

hints: Substitute L = 0.800 m and T = 1.80 s into g = 4 * pi^2 * L / T^2.
T is squared, so multiply its percentage uncertainty by 2 and add to % in L.
delta g = (% in g / 100) * g. Round delta g to 1 or 2 sig figs and match decimal places.
9702_t01_cm04_l08_theory09_b_iii.solution: delta g = 0.01362 * 9.748 = 0.133 m s^-2. Rounding to 1 sig fig gives 0.1 m s^-2, so g = (9.8 +/- 0.1) m s^-2 (or to 2 sig figs: (9.75 +/- 0.13) m s^-2).

mark_scheme: (a)(i) [1 mark]: T = 1.80 s and delta T = 0.01 s.
(a)(ii) [2 marks]: 1 mark for % in L = 0.25%; 1 mark for % in T = 0.56% (or 0.556%).
(b)(iii) [1 mark]: delta g = 0.13 m s^-2, final value (9.8 +/- 0.1) m s^-2 or (9.75 +/- 0.13) m s^-2.
hints: Divide timing measurements by 20 to get single-oscillation values.
T is squared in the formula for g, so its percentage uncertainty is doubled.
teacher_walkthrough: Step 1: Part (a)(i): compute T = 36.0 / 20 = 1.80 s and delta T = 0.2 / 20 = 0.01 s (1 mark).
Step 3: Part (b)(i): substitute into g formula: g = 4 * pi^2 * 0.800 / 1.80^2 = 9.75 m s^-2 (1 mark).
